newsitem.title: UK: BA attacks non-cooperation of cabin crew.
newsitem.headline: BA attacks non-cooperation of cabin crew.

text.p: British Airways Plc chief executive Bob Ayling said on Tuesday he saw a swift end to a dispute with ground staff but attacked cabin crew for a lack of cooperation in a separate dispute.
"I don't think there is actually any difficulty in resolving the catering issue (with ground staff)," Ayling told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
"I think there is a willingness in the area to resolve the issue...and I think it could be resolved very quickly, in two or three days."
"But the union which represents many of our cabin crew, BASSA, is a union we haven't had good relations with for a long time," he added.

"And when Bill (TGWU union general secretary Bill Morris) says to me in his letter that they cooperate with restructuring, I frankly don't recognise that cooperation with those people in the cabin crew area," he added.
BA faces the damaging prospect of industrial action on two fronts during the peak summer season.
Ground staff voted on Monday in favour of strike action in a dispute over BA plans to sell off its catering arm.
Cabin crew have voted for a series of 72-hour strikes in their five-month-old dispute over pay and conditions.
The two issues are separate but both are linked to BA's attempts to save 1.0 billion pounds by 2000 in a cost-cutting drive.
The TGWU's Morris said he wanted talks with BA's Ayling on both issues, saying there was no point in "solving half the problem".

"I'm prepared to meet Bob at any place, any time to deal with both disputes. You cannot discriminate one with another and that's the problem. He's trying to pick off the cabin crew against another group of workers," Morris told the BBC.

"Why is that intelligent, loyal people...the epitome of middle England suddenly decided they have had enough?..Let's resolve these two disputes and let's look at the wider and long-term implications," he added. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
